title: Stream a DJI drone without setting up NGINX and OBS (2026)
description: The usual way to get DJI Fly into OBS is an NGINX RTMP server, a config file and a media source. Here is what that setup involves, and the one-app way to skip it.
h1: Stream a DJI drone without setting up NGINX and OBS
lead: Search for how to get a DJI drone into OBS and most guides start the same way: install an NGINX RTMP server, edit its config, open the firewall, point DJI Fly at it and pull the stream into OBS as a media source. It works, but it is a small server project. DJI Live Bridge puts the RTMP server, the preview, the encoding and the platform outputs in one app — and can still hand the picture to OBS when you want it.
summary: The classic recipe is DJI Fly → NGINX with the RTMP module → OBS media source → one platform.
It means installing a server, editing nginx.conf, allowing port 1935 and building a scene by hand.
Several platforms at once needs an OBS plugin or a cloud service; a vertical canvas needs more setup.
DJI Live Bridge receives DJI Fly directly and streams to several platforms, vertical or horizontal, with nothing else installed.
If you want OBS anyway, Prepare OBS scene builds a DJI LIVE scene with the drone feed for you.

steps.d: NGINX with the RTMP module (on Windows often a prebuilt bundle), or another RTMP server.
Add an rtmp block with an application such as live to nginx.conf and start the server.
Allow incoming connections on port 1935 and find the computer's local address.
Enter something like rtmp://192.168.1.20/live/drone under Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP.
Add a Media Source with the same address, size it on the canvas, then set OBS's stream URL and key for your platform.

blocks.p: After that, every change is manual: a new network means a new address, a second platform means a plugin or a relay service, and a vertical stream means a second canvas or a separate profile.

blocks.p: OBS is unbeatable for scenes, overlays and transitions. DJI Live Bridge does not replace that — it replaces the NGINX part. Enable OBS WebSocket (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings), connect it in the app's Advanced tab and press Prepare OBS scene: the app creates a scene named DJI LIVE with the drone feed already in it, sized to a horizontal or vertical canvas.

blocks.note: For calls in Zoom, Meet or Teams through OBS Virtual Camera, see the webcam guide.

faq.q: Do I need NGINX to stream a DJI drone to OBS?
faq.a: No. DJI Live Bridge contains its own RTMP server; with Prepare OBS scene it also puts the drone feed into OBS without NGINX.

faq.q: Do I need OBS to stream a DJI drone?
faq.a: No. DJI Live Bridge streams to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other platforms directly. OBS is optional for scenes and overlays.
It works and is flexible, but you maintain a server, a config file and an OBS scene yourself, and multistreaming or vertical video need extra steps.

faq.q: What does DJI Live Bridge cost?
faq.a: Nothing. It is free and open source under the MIT licence.
